name: Hou Zi Ba Pi
description: Hou Zi Ba Pi (猴子扒皮 - literally 'Monkey Stripping the Skin') is an aggressive Chinese shedding game, often considered a variant of Big Two (Choi Dai Di). It is known for its fast-paced nature and the use of the term 'Monkey' as slang for specific high cards or the act of stripping an opponent's hand of its high cards.
alsoKnownAs: Hou Zi variant of Big Two

overview.description: Hou Zi Ba Pi (猴子扒皮 - literally 'Monkey Stripping the Skin') is an aggressive Chinese shedding game, often considered a variant of Big Two (Choi Dai Di). It is known for its fast-paced nature and the use of the term 'Monkey' as slang for specific high cards or the act of stripping an opponent's hand of its high cards.

history.origins: Derived from the Cantonese game 'Choi Dai Di' (Big Two). The 'Hou Zi' name surfaced in regional gambling circles, potentially referring to the speed of the game or the 'monkeying around' with high-value face cards.
timeline: 20th Century: Big Two variations spread across China.
1990s: 'Hou Zi' slang becomes prominent in specific poker clubs.
Present: Played digitally and in social circles under various regional names.
history.cultural: Reflects the competitive and humorous nature of Chinese social card play.
history.evolution: The game prioritizes 'power plays' where huge five-card combinations are used to quickly deplete one's hand, leaving opponents 'naked' or 'skinned' (Ba Pi).

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: 2 (High), A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3 (Low). Suits: Spades > Hearts > Clubs > Diamonds.

rules.objective: Be the first player to discard all cards in your hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. The player with the 3 of Diamonds starts (must play it in the first combination).
2. Players must play a higher card or combination than the previous player.
3. Types of plays: Single, Pair, Three-of-a-kind, Five-card combinations (Straight, Flush, Full House, Four-of-a-kind + 1, Straight Flush).
4. **Stripping (Ba Pi)**: If you play a combination that no one can beat, you 'strip' the lead and start the next round with any combination.
keyRules: Player with 3♦ must play it in the first combination.
Plays must match the number of cards led and rank higher (2 high, 3 low; Spades > Hearts > Clubs > Diamonds for ties).
Five-card combinations: Straight, Flush, Full House, Four-of-a-kind+1, Straight Flush.
When all others pass, the last player to play leads the next round with any combination.

strategy.basic: Keep high 2s and Aces to regain the lead. Don't waste your only high card on a low-value single.
strategy.intermediate: Shape your hand into five-card combinations early. A single 13-card hand is often won by 2 five-card plays and 3 singles.
strategy.advanced: The 'Monkey' tactic: Bait opponents into playing their 2 of Spades early so you can dominate the endgame with your Aces.
tips: Always track which 2s have been played.
If you have many small singles, try to build a Full House to get rid of 5 cards at once.
